## PART 2: REGIONAL PLAYBOOKS WITH EXECUTION DETAIL

### 2.1 EU WORKER COUNCIL MODEL (Mandatory Co-Decision)

**Strategic Objective:** Establish legitimate worker representation via elected multi-country council; negotiate binding agreements on wages, deactivation, algorithms, safety; maintain platform operational authority on pricing, routing, profitability targets.

#### **Governance Structure in Depth**

**EU Worker Council (Platform-Wide, Multi-Country)**

**Composition & Electoral Process:**

| Country | Seats | Worker Population | Electoral Method | Union Role |
|---------|-------|---|---|---|
| **Germany** | 5 | 12,000–15,000 riders | Secret ballot; one vote per active worker; top vote-getters fill seats | Union can sponsor candidates; no monopoly |
| **France** | 3 | 8,000–10,000 riders | Secret ballot; proportional representation (if multiple unions/groups organize, seats distributed by vote share) | Union sponsorship allowed |
| **Italy** | 3 | 6,000–8,000 riders | Secret ballot; if <30% turnout, second round held; independent + union candidates equally marketed | Union role proportional to historical organizing |
| **Spain** | 2 | 4,000–5,000 riders | Secret ballot | Union role proportional |
| **Belgium** | 1 | 2,000–3,000 riders | Secret ballot | Union role proportional |
| **Other EU (rotating)** | 2 | 5,000–7,000 riders (Poland, Netherlands, Portugal, etc.) | Rotating annual representation; one seat per year rotates among countries with 500+ riders | Regional rotation ensures broader voice |

**Total Seats:** 16–18 elected representatives

**Electoral Timeline (Annual, Q1):**
- **Months 1–2:** Candidate recruitment; independent + union candidates publicize platforms
- **Month 3, Week 1–2:** Voting window (2-week period, voting via app + paper ballot option for non-digital workers)
- **Month 3, Week 3:** Ballot count (external election administrator verifies; results announced)
- **Month 4, Week 1:** Council orientation + first plenary meeting

**Voter Eligibility:** Active rider status in past 6 months; account in good standing (no fraud allegations pending)

**Candidate Eligibility:** Active rider in past 12 months; no platform management role in past 2 years; no conflict of interest (e.g., family member in senior management); signed code of conduct (confidentiality, ethical behavior)

**Campaign Support (Platform Responsibility):** Equal funding for candidate marketing (e.g., $2K per candidate in app notifications, email, posters); platform remains neutral (no endorsements); union candidates receive same support as independents

**Conflict-of-Interest Protocols:**
- Councilors cannot receive special pay/benefits beyond other workers; cannot take platform management roles during term
- If conflict emerges (e.g., councilor's family member promoted to senior role), councilor must recuse from decisions affecting that area
- External ethics advisor (retired labor law judge, $10K retainer) available if conflict dispute arises

**Meeting Structure & Authority:**

| Meeting Type | Frequency | Attendees | Quorum | Decision Authority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Plenary (Full Council)** | Monthly (2-day in-person, rotating EU city) | 16–18 elected members + Platform facilitator + Council secretary + External labor relations advisor (observer only, can provide input) | 60% (10–11 members) | Plenary approves all council positions; 2/3 majority required for co-decision positions (wage bands, deactivation, algorithms, safety) |
| **Sub-Committee (4 committees)** | Bi-weekly (virtual, 2-hour sessions) | 4–5 councilors per committee + committee facilitator + topic expert (e.g., safety officer, finance analyst) | 60% committee membership | Recommendations to plenary; plenary votes on final position |
| **Emergency Plenary** | As needed (within 48 hours of trigger) | All 16–18 members | Simple majority quorum | Addresses urgent issues (media crisis, litigation threat, major incident); decisions documented; ratified at next regular plenary |
| **Bilateral (Chair + Platform Lead)** | Bi-weekly (1-hour call) | Council chair + CPO or Regional Labor Relations Director | N/A | Information sharing; identifies blocking issues pre-meeting; no binding decisions |

**Sub-Committees (Specialized Authority):**

1. **Wages & Compensation Committee (4 members, one per major country)**
   - **Scope:** Negotiates annual wage band (min/max delivery price, geographic variations, incentive caps); reviews wage variance against peer regions; investigates wage discrimination complaints
   - **Authority:** Recommends wage bands to full plenary; plenary vote required; 2/3 majority threshold for approval
   - **Escalation:** If platform rejects council-approved wage band, external mediator consulted; mediator recommends compromise; platform decides with documented rationale
   - **Frequency:** Monthly meetings; annual wage review cycle (September–November) for January implementation

2. **Deactivation & Appeals Committee (4 members)**
   - **Scope:** Defines deactivation criteria (rating thresholds, acceptance rates, safety violations, fraud); designs appeal process; reviews deactivation rate trends; investigates appeals for bias
   - **Authority:** Designs deactivation policy; platform co-approves (binding); reviews sample deactivation cases monthly (5–10 anonymized cases) to ensure criteria applied consistently
   - **Escalation:** If appeal reversal rate drops below council expectation (e.g., <5% appeals overturned), committee can demand policy review
   - **Frequency:** Monthly case review meetings; quarterly policy review

3. **Algorithms & Data Committee (4 members, ideally with technical literacy)**
   - **Scope:** Specifies scope of external algorithmic audit (which algorithms, what metrics, frequency); selects/approves external auditor; reviews audit findings; demands explanations of algorithmic decisions
   - **Authority:** Co-designs audit scope; platform implements with minor modifications only; council approves external auditor selection from pre-approved list
   - **Escalation:** If audit reveals bias or unexplained variance, committee can demand remediation plan; non-compliance triggers public disclosure option
   - **Frequency:** Quarterly audit scope planning; annual external audit; ad-hoc emergency audits if bias complaint emerges

4. **Safety & Working Conditions Committee (4 members)**
   - **Scope:** Sets minimum safety standards (equipment, training, incident response, insurance); reviews safety incident reports monthly; investigates safety complaints; demands corrective actions
   - **Authority:** Co-designs safety standards (binding co-decision); quarterly review of incidents; can demand safety improvements (e.g., "helmets required," "first-aid training 2x/year," "insurance premium increased")
   - **Escalation:** If safety incidents rise above historical baseline, committee can demand emergency safety audit; suspension of high-risk routes if necessary
   - **Frequency:** Monthly safety incident review; quarterly safety standard review

**Secretariat Support:**

- **Council Administrator** (1 FTE, hired by council, budgeted by platform, reports to council chair): Manages meeting logistics, transcription, minutes, document repository, public communications
- **External Facilitator** (contract, 8 hours/month): Facilitates conflict resolution in sub-committees; mediates councilor disagreements; no binding authority, but expertise valued
- **Operating Budget:** $80K–$120K/year (administrator salary $60K–$75K + meetings/travel $20K–$30K + facilitation/training $5K–$10K)

---

#### **Scope of Authority (Detailed)**

**BINDING CO-DECISION (Council Veto Equivalent—2/3 Majority Required):**

1. **Annual Wage Band Review (September–November, effective January):**

   - **Platform proposes:** Annual wage band structure:
     - **Base delivery rates:** Min $X–Max $Y per delivery (varies by city/region, e.g., €5.50–€7.50 in Berlin, €4.80–€6.80 in Budapest)
     - **Incentive cap:** Max incentive as % of base (e.g., +30% for acceptance rate >90%, +20% for safety record)
     - **Peak/off-peak multipliers:** e.g., 1.2x during 11am–1pm, 1.0x off-peak
     - **Variance permitted by region:** max 10% variance between similar cities (Germany vs. Austria, for example)
   
   - **Council negotiates:** Typically 2–3 rounds of offers/counteroffers (September: platform proposal → October: council feedback + revised proposal → November: council vote)
   
   - **Approval criteria (Council must assess):**
     - Is wage sufficient for living costs + benefits adequacy in each region?
     - Is wage increase (if any) justified by platform profitability trends?
     - Are incentive caps fair (do they incentivize quality without creating perverse outcomes, e.g., cherry-picking high-value deliveries)?
   
   - **If unresolved after 2 rounds:**
     - External mediator (pre-identified labor law expert) convened
     - Mediator hears both sides; recommends compromise wage band
     - Recommendation non-binding, but carries weight with EU regulators if dispute escalates to labor ministry
     - Platform makes final decision; if rejected mediator recommendation, documented rationale provided
   
   - **Wage band locked for 12 months;** platform cannot reduce mid-year without council consent (mid-year increase possible if platform profitability >15% above forecast)
   
   - **Council can demand wage review if:**
     - Inflation >3% (annual CPI adjustment triggered automatically)
     - Platform profitability >15% above forecast (triggers mandatory profit-sharing discussion)
     - Deactivation rate spike (wage insufficient → workers become inactive → demand to investigate root cause)

   - **Precedent:** Previous year's wage band becomes floor (no wage cuts permitted year-over-year without council consent)

2. **Deactivation Policy (Criteria, Process, Appeal):**

   - **Platform proposes:** Deactivation criteria:
     - **Customer ratings:** Deactivate if rolling 30-day avg rating <3.5/5.0 (platform can justify threshold via historical data)
     - **Acceptance rate:** Deactivate if <60% over 30 days (but must provide 48-hour warning + opportunity to improve)
     - **Safety violations:** Automatic deactivation for helmet non-compliance, insurance lapse, fraud, unsafe route violations
     - **Response time:** Deactivate if response to 3+ batch offers <30 seconds (indicates app malfunction or abandonment)
   
   - **Council negotiates:** Typically demands stricter due process:
     - "Deactivation is last resort; performance improvement plan must precede deactivation (except fraud/safety)"
     - "48-hour notice of pending deactivation mandatory; exception only for active safety threat"
     - "Appeal window expanded to 10 days (not 7 days); human review mandatory for all appeals"
     - "Deactivation criteria cannot change mid-year without council consent"
   
   - **Approval criteria:**
     - Is due process fair? (Does worker get warning + opportunity to improve?)
     - Are criteria objective and consistently applied? (No manager discretion; automated systems audited for bias)
     - Is appeal process credible? (Human reviewer has authority to overturn algorithmic deactivation?)
   
   - **Appeal metrics tracked & reviewed monthly:**
     - % of appeals reversed (platform target: 5–10%; <5% suggests criteria too strict or appeal process invalid)
     - % of reversals where worker returns to active status (if >70% successfully return, suggests deactivation was premature)
     - Demographic analysis of deactivations (council can demand explanation if certain demographic deactivated at higher rate)
   
   - **Council authority to revise policy mid-year if:**
     - Deactivation rate rises >10% above historical baseline (triggers investigation: criteria too strict? Or worker quality declining?)
     - Appeal reversal rate falls below 5% (suggests appeal process not credible)

3. **Algorithmic Audit Scope & External Auditor Selection:**

   - **Council specifies algorithms subject to annual audit:**
     - Rating/review system: Does algo amplify certain rating types? Is review moderation consistent?
     - Batch allocation: Do certain rider demographics receive fewer/lower-value batches? Is allocation truly random or biased?
     - Surge pricing: Does surge price correlate with rider demographics? Are certain areas overcharged during peak?
     - Acceptance incentives: Are incentive structures equally transparent for all riders?
   
   - **Audit scope negotiated annually (Q4):**
     - Council selects auditor from pre-approved list (labor law firm, academic institution, independent audit firm; criteria: labor-law expertise, algorithmic literacy, independence from platform)
     - Audit budget: $75K–$120K/year (platform funds, council selects; competitive bids if necessary)
     - Audit timeline: 8–12 weeks; report delivered by June 1 for discussion at summer plenary
   
   - **Audit findings (Redacted for Trade Secrets, Core Findings Disclosed):**
     - Executive summary (1–2 pages, public-facing): Key findings, recommendations, remediation timeline
     - Detailed report (confidential, council + platform + external advisor only): Algorithm code (redacted), bias analysis, statistical findings
     - Council briefing: Auditor presents findings; platform responds with remediation plan within 30 days
   
   - **Non-Compliance Escalation:**
     - If audit reveals algorithmic bias (e.g., "women riders receive batches worth €50/hour avg, men €65/hour"), council can demand:
       - Root-cause analysis by platform data scientists
       - Remediation plan (adjust algorithm, back-pay affected riders, etc.)
       - Timeline for fix (typically 60 days)
       - Quarterly verification audits to confirm fix
     - If platform refuses remediation, council can escalate to German labor ministry (co-determination law authority) or demand public disclosure (reputational risk to platform)

4. **Safety Standards (Mandatory Minimums—Binding Co-Decision):**

   - **Platform proposes baseline standards:**
     - Helmets: Provided/subsidized (€30–€50 value); replacement if damaged
     - Visibility vests: Reflective vests required during night shifts; platform provides
     - First-aid training: Annual, mandatory (platform funds via third-party trainer)
     - Accident insurance: Platform-paid, €500K+ coverage; covers injuries while actively delivering
     - Emergency protocols: Panic button on app (direct line to emergency services + platform), reporting procedure for incidents, medical follow-up protocol
   
   - **Council negotiates & approves (typically demands enhancements):**
     - "Insurance must cover commute to/from delivery, not just active deliveries"
     - "First-aid training 2x/year, not 1x/year, in winter months (highest accident rate)"
     - "Helmet replacement budget increased to cover 3 replacements/year (current 1)"
     - "Weather safety: Deliveries suspended if temperature <-5°C or wind gusts >60 km/h (council-approved weather thresholds)"
   
   - **Council monitors quarterly:**
     - Safety incident rate (injuries per 100K deliveries)
     - Equipment compliance (% of riders with valid helmet/vest)
     - Training completion rates
     - Insurance claims processed (average payout time)
   
   - **Council authority to demand enhancements mid-year if:**
     - Incident rate rises 10%+ above quarterly average
     - Training completion drops below 95%
     - Insurance claims stall (average payout time >30 days)

---

**CONSULTATION (Council Input, Platform Decides):**

1. **Pricing Strategy & Dynamic Pricing:**
   - Platform briefs council quarterly on pricing strategy changes (e.g., "introducing surge pricing during 11am–1pm lunch rush; multiplier 1.3x base rate")
   - Council provides feedback; can request pilot test in one city before rollout to all
   - Platform decides final implementation; must document council input + explain any divergence from council recommendation
   - Helps defend strategy if workers protest ("Council was consulted and approved overall approach")

2. **Feature Launches (Batch Size, Routing, Incentive Changes):**
   - Platform briefs council 4 weeks pre-launch on new features (e.g., "Shrinking batch size from 5 to 3 deliveries/batch to improve speed")
   - Council can request 2-week pilot in limited market before full rollout
   - Council feedback incorporated if feasible; documented rationale if not
   - Post-launch: Council monitors worker sentiment (complaints, deactivation rate, app usage); demands adjustment if negative impact evident

3. **Expansion to New EU Countries:**
   - Platform consults council on labor landscape, union strength, regulatory risk before entry
   - Council assesses organizing risk; flags countries where strong unions likely to demand immediate council establishment
   - Council provides early warning; platform adjusts entry strategy (e.g., accelerate council formation in Germany vs. delay in Portugal if organizing likely)

4. **Contractor Reclassification (If Considered):**
   - If platform considers moving toward employee status (partial or full), platform consults council on implications
   - Council negotiates new terms (salary structure, benefits, scheduling, job security)
   - This is consultation stage; council cannot veto, but council negotiating power strong (reclassification has major implications; council buy-in valuable for legitimacy)

---

**INFORMATION RIGHTS (Council Notified, No Veto):**

1. **Monthly Dashboard (Shared with Council, Public Aggregated Summary)**
   - Deactivation rates (by country, by reason, trending)
   - Appeal outcomes (# appeals, # reversals, % reversal rate)
   - Safety incidents (count, severity, resolution status)
   - Wage variance analysis (min/max rates, regional variation %)
   - Customer complaints related to worker safety (anonymized themes)

2. **Quarterly Briefings**
   - Platform profitability (revenue, COGS, labor cost %)
   - Litigation status (any lawsuits filed, case status)
   - Regulatory changes (new labor law, government inquiry, labor ministry action)
   - Market conditions (competition, volume trends, customer acquisition cost)
   - Context: Helps council understand budget constraints ("Why can't we increase wages 10%? Because profitability down 8% YoY due to competitive pricing")

3. **Annual Transparency Report (Public-Facing)**
   - Council composition (member names, election results)
   - Wage bands negotiated (annual ranges, changes from prior year, justification)
   - Deactivation policy (criteria, process, appeal outcomes, samples of overturned appeals)
   - Safety incidents (count, types, remediation actions)
   - Algorithmic audit (summary of findings, remediation completed)
   - Council accomplishments (e.g., "Council negotiated 5% wage increase, expanded insurance coverage to commute time, implemented bi-weekly safety training")
   - Builds worker trust ("Council delivers tangible wins") + defends
